observations: Photo shows a large white chest-style freezer/cold box with a metal latch on top front.
A label on the front panel is visible and includes text: “120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION”.
No clear brand name or model number is readable in the photo.
No power cord, rating plate, or interior view is shown.
Seller text overlay in the image (“POSTED ON JJJ-KICKS”) appears to be watermark/branding, not product specs.

claims.evidence: The photo shows “120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION” but does not clearly show “250-liter” or a capacity marking.
No voltage range/rating plate is readable in the photo.
Photo 0 front label clearly shows “120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION”.
Photo 0 shows the unit but provides no power-on test, temperature reading, or running compressor evidence.

risks.risk: Capacity/size may not be 250L (pricing depends heavily on volume).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rating/capacity label (or model plate) showing liters, plus a tape-measure of external dimensions.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used chest freezer/cold box with unknown capacity (worst-case: smaller/less valuable unit).

risks.risk: Not actually working (compressor/thermostat/fan may be faulty).
risks.proof: Video of the unit plugged in and running (compressor sound), plus a thermometer reading after 30–60 minutes.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working/needs repair until proven working.

risks.risk: Cooling retention claim may be marketing; insulation condition could be poor (dents, seal gaps).
risks.proof: Photo of door gasket/seals and interior condition; then a timed temperature drop test (start temp vs after 2–4 hours).
risks.if_unproven: Price as reduced performance (worst-case: retention not reliable).

risks.risk: Low-voltage compatibility may be incorrect (could require stabilizer or may trip).
risks.proof: Photo of electrical rating plate showing voltage range, and a test at the stated low voltage (or with a stabilizer) while running.
risks.if_unproven: Price as standard-voltage only (assume low-voltage claim unverified).

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rating/model plate showing brand, model, and capacity (liters).
Video proof the unit is powered on and cooling (compressor running) with a thermometer reading after 30–60 minutes.
Close-up photos of the door gasket/seals and any visible dents/rust.
Photo of electrical specifications (voltage range) to confirm “low voltage operation”.
response.reason: The photo supports only the “120 hours cooling retention” text, but capacity, low-voltage operation, and “working condition” are not proven. Without a power-on test and the capacity/model plate, a safe worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
